counterfactual_rationale: The ROCm/MoRI failure comes from idle DP-attention ranks launching zero-sized kernels and a mismatched collective path. Edge tests with zero-token ranks under DP attention on HIP would plausibly expose it.

The AITER persistent MLA decode metadata gate omitted the nhead=64 TP2 DeepSeek-R1 case, causing memory faults. Configuration tests over per-rank head counts 32, 64, and 128 on AMD hardware would plausibly catch it.
The QK-norm helper crashed only when Dynamo traced it during piecewise CUDA-graph warmup. A torch.compile plus piecewise-CUDA-graph startup test for Qwen3 QK-norm would plausibly expose it.

The fix maps logical, redundant, and shared experts correctly for EPLB with Waterfill, a layout hard to validate from isolated kernels. An EP redundant-expert serving or accuracy test would plausibly reveal the mis-mapping.

The wrong results require multi-prompt chunked prefill where some rows have kv_len=0 while others continue. Edge tests with varied prefix lengths on Blackwell trtllm_mla would plausibly catch the stale zero-length rows.
The ROCm AITER dependency changed an enum in a breaking way, requiring a fused-MoE patch after updating the commit. ROCm/AITER version-matrix CI would plausibly expose the incompatibility.

The trtllm-gen MLA path consumed an empty-initialized decode CUDA-graph workspace, so stale values could affect accuracy. Initcheck-style validation or an accuracy test comparing zeroed and empty workspaces would plausibly reveal it.

The sampler crashed only when nan detection was enabled against the updated FlashInfer sampling API. A serving or sampler integration test with use_nan_detection enabled would plausibly hit the variable/signature error.

The JIT namespace migration broke first-use compilation for the single-token MoE and diffusion modulation kernels without changing their math. Fresh-cache JIT tests for those kernels would plausibly catch the missing namespace.

The GDN CUDA-graph metadata and causal_conv1d stride bug surfaced in Qwen3-Next MTP serving with particular speculative-token settings. A CUDA-graph/spec-decode integration matrix for GDN models would plausibly expose it.

The GPU fault appears only with DP attention and max concurrency above 256, due to metadata mode for mla_decode_fwd. Stress tests varying concurrency and DP-attention metadata on AMD would plausibly trigger it.

The stale CUDA-graph track-buffer tail corrupts logits only after decode, cache insertion, and a later prefix-hit rescore. Invariance checks comparing cold prefill with graphed cache-hit rescoring would plausibly catch the KL divergence.

The CustomAllReduceV2 capture path failed only when NVLink was unavailable and the object field was absent. CI that includes non-NVL CUDA topology during CUDA-graph capture would plausibly expose the AttributeError.
The router replay capture buffer stayed zero or captured post-EPLB physical expert IDs instead of logical IDs. A router-replay integration test with EPLB enabled would plausibly reveal the mismatch.

The fix concerns global and local expert counts at weight creation for EP after a previous MoE change. EP configuration tests that vary global/local expert counts would plausibly expose the bad layout.

The trtllm-MoE FP4 renormalization issue affected specific DeepSeek and Qwen NVFP4 model families. Real quantized-model accuracy tests are more plausible than generic random tests for catching the renorm regression.
The CUDA 11.8 build failed because kernels unsupported before CUDA 12 were still built and FlashInfer AOT settings were wrong. A CUDA-version build matrix would plausibly catch the failure.

The shape mismatch occurs for DSA prefill with CP, fp8 KV cache, and trtllm when KV is gathered before fused RoPE quantization. A CP-split and KV-dtype configuration matrix on B300/GB300 would plausibly expose it.

The CutlassMLA implementation lacked a workspace buffer only under the TRTLLM ragged DeepSeek prefill path. A serving startup test with that environment flag and DeepSeek model would plausibly catch the AttributeError.

The FusedMoE weight loader failed when EP backends padded hidden_size for alignment but checkpoint weights kept the original size. Unit tests varying padded hidden dimensions would plausibly expose the copy_ mismatch.

The ROCm RMSNorm reduction was not batch-invariant under deterministic inference, causing logprob wobble across batch compositions. Determinism tests that vary batch and prefix composition would plausibly catch it.

The FlashInfer A2A/MoE BF16 path resolved crashes and invalid-argument cases such as zero DP tokens per rank. A full DP-attention plus EP-MoE serving test, including zero-token ranks, would plausibly expose it.
The NaN appears only for draft-extend CUDA-graph metadata at topk>1 and bs>1 because qo_indptr uses the wrong stride. Edge tests over topk and batch size for EAGLE spec-v2 would plausibly expose it.

The EXAONE head_dim=80 configuration requested the Triton backend but still hit FlashInfer unsupported-head-dim behavior. Backend-selection tests with uncommon head dimensions would plausibly catch the rotary embedding issue.

The aiter/DeepEP shared-expert scaling bug barely affected short GSM8K but caused long-form runaway repetition and large MLPerf accuracy loss. Long-output realistic workloads would plausibly reveal the under-weighted shared expert.
